title: Blues in Texas versus elsewhere; Lee Collins
summary: They discuss why Lips and Kennedy played little blues and how Texas blues differed. Albert credits Lee Collins and Guy Kelly with bringing blues.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Well what sort of blues could these guys play?
Really Lips didn't play much blues? Not too much blues. Not too much blues.
He was very excited. He was an exciting trumpet player.
That's what he was. So was Claude Kennedy.

I wondered because, you see, some guys I listen to, and I'm not mixing in any names, or any names, or any names. Well, the whole areas of the country, you didn't hear good blues from them. Whereas I hear Texas had good blues, you know. And you go back and you hear early New Orleans guys, to me they sounded like good blues players.

It was a different type of blues in Texas. You had, I can't recall the name of all of these players, you would have to come back to them. But Claude Kennedy was part of his clan, but he didn't lay on the blues. Now the fella that really brought some blues to Texas was a trumpet player from here, that died not so long ago in Chicago, maybe quite a few years ago, Lee Collins. That was another great technician. And Guy Kelly, which was no relation to Chris, those fellas had, they had some dreams, I'd say. A man has to dream to play what those guys were.
